text:
mike: gitops apply failed on gpu-pool (eu-west-1) for PR #342, CI error below:

mike: ```
Error: Error locking state: Error acquiring the state lock: ConditionalCheckFailedException: The conditional request failed
  on backend.DynamoDB
```

sre-bot: deployment-ci: apply failed for infra/gpu-pool (run id: 2026-03-18T10:05Z). logs: https://ci.redwood/integrations/342/logs

alex: seeing a stale entry in tf-locks DynamoDB: LockID=5a2b7f8c-... created_at=2026-03-18T09:50Z. looks like previous apply aborted.

priya: we did a state move yesterday (split gpu_pools into a dedicated module). I ran: `terraform state mv module.cluster.module.gpu_pools module.gpu_pools` from my laptop. Could that have left inconsistent state metadata?

cheng: check backend path first: `s3://redwood-tfstate/eu-west-1/infra.tfstate`. run `terraform state pull` and inspect `serial`/`lineage`. If the lineage changed during move it can confuse locks. Also query dynamodb: `aws dynamodb get-item --table-name tf-locks --key '{"LockID":{"S":"5a2b7f8c-..."}}'`

alex: don't force-unlock unless we confirm no apply is active. if CI runner is still alive it could corrupt state. @mike can you confirm no other pipeline is currently applying?

mike: confirmed. other runners finished earlier. safe to proceed.

alex: ok i'll run from ci-ops host: `terraform force-unlock 5a2b7f8c-...` then re-trigger the gitops job. Will post back.

alex: unlocked, re-triggering gitops apply now.

priya: FYI during the state move I changed the workspace to `prod-eu` in the pipeline matrix. double-check `terraform workspace show` on the runner; workspace mismatch can create different state keys/locks.

cheng: adding a note to runbook: 1) check `terraform workspace show` 2) confirm `terraform state pull | jq .lineage` and `terraform state list | head` before force-unlock. Also added a small script to scan for stale locks older than 24h and print associated serial/owner as a dry-run.

mike: apply went through on re-run, pools are provisioning. will watch capacity metrics for the next 15m.

alex: if we see repeat occurrences we should consider switching CI to a central apply orchestrator (single serial apply) or use consul-based locks.

priya: also logging this in infra-runbook issue tracker: https://issues.redwood/INFRA-678 (state-move followup + lock hygiene).

cheng: short-term mitigation: add `preflight` check in gitops job that fails early if `aws dynamodb get-item` shows a lock younger than 2h.

mike: great. thanks all :thumbsup:
